gaps: Does the psutil port preserve the PID-reuse identity guard the old lstart check provided?
Can the Windows launch path be verified in this stage (macOS/POSIX only here)?
Does dropping preexec_fn lose any needed child-process setup?
resolutions: Yes — identity moves from lstart-string to create_time() float; the guard is preserved: never signal a PID whose create_time differs from the recorded one. reviewer_focus pins it.

No — this stage is POSIX-verifiable (the port must be observably byte-identical on POSIX; ps-monkeypatch tests migrate to psutil fakes). The genuinely-Windows launch/reap E2E is WIN-3.2, verified on windows-hook-gates CI.

No — preexec_fn only ran unblock_termination_signals_in_child (pthread_sigmask unblock), which is already a no-op where pthread_sigmask is absent; the signal arming/restore in the parent is unchanged. Dropping preexec_fn removes a Windows-raising call with no POSIX behavior loss.
